text:
maria: Heads-up — noticed a SCIM deprovision lag on the Azure group-sync job. Two ex-employees still show up in the 'dedicated-admins' group after the nightly run. :exclamation:

helena: Which job? group-sync or the SCIM push from Azure AD? Any error lines from the job? :eyes:

maria: It's the azure -> our SCIM bridge (group-sync). Job started at 2026-03-18T04:00Z and finished, but the deprovision queue shows entries. Quick paste of the tail of the sync log:
```
2026-03-18T04:02:13Z WARN  scim-sync: failed to remove member user=jane.doe@ex.com group=dedicated-admins http_status=429 err='rate_limited'
2026-03-18T04:02:13Z INFO  scim-sync: enqueuing deprovision job id=ddb-045 retry=0
2026-03-18T04:02:14Z ERROR scim-sync: deprovision-worker id=ddb-045 status=queued_for_retry last_err='429 Too Many Requests'
```

maria: Looks like 429s caused a backlog and the worker didn't retry aggressively (backoff policy seems no-op).

scim-bot: last successful full sync: 2026-03-17T04:00:02Z. pending_deprovisions=2

aj: Did we change any role or group name mappings last week? I remember a permissions refactor where we renamed 'dedicated-admins' -> 'dedicated-admins-v2' in the RBAC mapping table. If the mapping is stale, the SCIM id -> internal role join might fail and leave accounts in the old role.

helena: Good call. Check the mapping table scim_group_map and the fallback logic in scim-processor. If group name doesn't match, we should still reconcile by scim_group_id.

samir: I'll take the pager. First step: confirm which users are still in the group and whether they have active sessions/tokens. Quick query I ran: 
```sql
SELECT email, last_login_at, membership_created_at FROM org_group_members WHERE group_name='dedicated-admins';
-- returns jane.doe@ex.com (last_login 2025-11-02), mike.old@ex.com (last_login 2024-08-10)
```

maria: exact — jane.doe and mike.old. jane had SSO disabled but still in group. mike.old definitely should've been removed months ago.

helena: Proposed hotfix: 1) manual deprovision of the two accounts from the group, 2) patch scim-sync to treat 429 as retryable with exponential backoff and a longer retry window, 3) add alert when pending_deprovisions > 0 for > 30m. Approve deploy?

aj: Approve the manual deprovision and the retry patch. Please add an audit log entry and ticket SEC-487 for follow-up tests.

samir: Performing manual deprovision via admin-cli now:
```bash
admin-cli groups remove-member --group dedicated-admins --member jane.doe@ex.com --actor samir
Response: OK 200 removed
admin-cli groups remove-member --group dedicated-admins --member mike.old@ex.com --actor samir
Response: OK 200 removed
```

oncall-bot: Deploy started by helena for scim-sync:patch/retry-429 -> staging at 2026-03-18T08:15Z :rocket:

maria: After manual removals and patch deploy, pending_deprovisions=0 and Azure shows both users not in group. Confirmed by audit log entry:
```
2026-03-18T08:16:05Z INFO audit: action=group_remove actor=samir target=jane.doe@ex.com group=dedicated-admins via=admin-cli
2026-03-18T08:16:10Z INFO audit: action=group_remove actor=samir target=mike.old@ex.com group=dedicated-admins via=admin-cli
```

helena: Thanks. Follow-ups: (a) add unit/integration test for mapping rename compatibility (scim_group_map fallback by scim_group_id), (b) add a monitor on scim deprovision queue age, (c) run a small postmortem and tag SEC-487. I'll own the follow-up.

aj: Also add a small runbook step to reprocess pending_deprovisions on 5xx/429 spikes.

maria: Closing the thread — root cause: rate-limiting + mapping fragility after permissions rename. Remediation: manual deprovision + retry patch + alerts. Leaving notes in SEC-487. :white_check_mark:
